key_features.classic_presentation: ONSET: GRADUAL onset over hours to days. LOCATION: UNILATERAL or bilateral kidney involvement. DURATION: Develops over hours to days, may persist for days to weeks. CHARACTER: FLANK pain, may have decreased urine output. AGGRAVATING: MOVEMENT, urination. RELIEVING: OBSTRUCTION relief, pain medications. TIMING: Gradual onset, develops over hours to days. SEVERITY: 5-8/10, moderate to severe. ASSOCIATED SYMPTOMS: FLANK PAIN, may have decreased urine output, may have fever if infected. KEY POSITIVES: Flank pain, positive imaging, may have decreased urine output. KEY NEGATIVES: No fever, no neck stiffness, no focal neurological deficits.

red_flags: Severe pain with fever - possible infected hydronephrosis, call 911
Signs of severe infection - fever, chills, rigors - call 911
Severe hypertension with neurological deficits - possible hypertensive crisis, call 911
Signs of severe metabolic acidosis - deep breathing, confusion, coma - call 911
Signs of severe electrolyte imbalances - confusion, seizures, cardiac arrhythmias - call 911
